title: 1980 AHSME Problem 7
statement: Sides \(AB,\) \(BC,\) \(CD,\) and \(DA\) of convex polygon \(ABCD\) have lengths \(3,\) \(4,\) \(12,\) and \(13,\) respectively; and \(\angle CBA\) is a right angle. The area of the quadrilateral is

solutions.text:
Triangle \(ABC\) is a \(3\)-\(4\)-\(5\) right triangle, so \(AC=5\) and its area is \(6.\) Since \(5^2+12^2=13^2,\) triangle \(ACD\) is right at \(C\) and has area \((\frac{1}{2})(5)(12)=30.\) The quadrilateral’s area is \(6+30=36.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Draw diagonal \(AC\) and find its length from \(\triangle ABC\)
Recognize a second right triangle using the side lengths \(5,\) \(12,\) and \(13\)
